\begin{bankq}[id=SI01-P1-PHY-S2-Q06, source={Score-I - Test 01 (16 Jun 2021)}, paper=1, qno=6, type=multi, subtopic={Energy}, answer={B,C,D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K1 S3 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: time taken by a bob sliding on two different curved surfaces | steps: energy gives same speed at the bottom; compare path lengths and speeds point by point; acceleration along path; time comparison; check options | I: compare the time on two paths with the same speed at equal heights}]
A small bob can slide downwards from point A to B along either of the two different curved surfaces shown in cross-section in the diagram. These possible trajectories are circular arcs in vertical plane, and they lie symmetrically about straight line AB. During the motion, bob does not leave contact with surface.
\bfig{70.7}{SI01_p1_phy_s2_q06_1.png}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{If friction is neglected every where bob will take a smaller time through path I as compared to time through path II.}
\opt{B}{If friction is neglected every where bob will take a smaller time through path II as compared to time through path I.}
\opt{C}{If friction is neglected every where bob will reach point B with same speed through both the paths.}
\opt{D}{If friction is significant along both paths then bob will reach B with a smaller speed, if it follows path II, as compared to if it follows path I.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SI03-P1-PHY-S1-Q07, source={Score-I - Test 03 (07 Jan 2022)}, paper=1, qno=7, type=multi, subtopic={Energy}, answer={A,D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: bead on a smooth vertical circular wire attached to a spring or string | steps: energy conservation; normal force from centripetal equation; speed at positions; check | I: normal force can change sign along the wire}]
A bead of mass $m$ can slide on a smooth circular wire of radius $a$, which is fixed in a vertical plane. The bead is connected to the highest point of the wire by a light spring of natural length $3a/2$ and spring constant $k$. P is lowest point on ring. Choose the CORRECT statement(s).
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{For bead, P is stable equilibrium position if $k=\dfrac{2mg}{a}$}
\opt{B}{For bead, P is unstable equilibrium position if $k=\dfrac{2mg}{a}$}
\opt{C}{For bead, P is stable equilibrium position if $k=\dfrac{5mg}{a}$}
\opt{D}{For bead, P is unstable equilibrium position if $k=\dfrac{5mg}{a}$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
